goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 uses String#scrub which requires Ruby 2.1 but Discourse runs on 1.9/2.0, raising NoMethodError and killing the PollFeed job every hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the new code does `i.content.scrub` before importing (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). `String#scrub` is not available on older Ruby versions (notably 1.9/2.0), so if Discourse is run on those versions this will raise `NoMethodError` and cause the scheduled `PollFeed` job to fail whenever it runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New gems ruby-readability and simple-rss added to Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock updated, breaking bundle install for environments using the main Gemfile.lock

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new gems added to Gemfile and corresponding entries added to Gemfile_rails4.lock. It does not show whether a separate main Gemfile.lock exists or is expected/used in other environments, so the claim that bundle install will break due to an un-updated Gemfile.lock cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 calls i.content.scrub but content is nil for plain RSS 2.0 feeds (which use description), crashing the poll job on the first non-Atom item
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core issue: `i.content.scrub` can crash when `i.content` is nil, especially for RSS 2.0 feeds that use `description` instead of `content`, implying the need for a fallback to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:41 relies on open-uri loaded incidentally by another file rather than requiring it directly, risking NoMethodError on 'open' if load ordering changes

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but the file does not `require 'open-uri'`. `open-uri` is only required in Jobs::PollFeed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), which may not be loaded before TopicEmbed is used (e.g., via TopicRetriever or the disqus.thor task). Without requiring `open-uri`, `open("http://...")` won’t fetch HTTP content and will instead behave like plain Kernel#open (likely raising a file-related error), so behavior depends on incidental load order.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:14 anonymous users never receive the throttle exemption (current_user.try(:id) is nil), so anonymous embed fetches get blocked by the 60s redis throttle and re-queued by the 30s reload

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists it enqueues `retrieve_topic` with `user_id: current_user.try(:id)`, which will be nil for anonymous users. In `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, the `no_throttle` option passed to `TopicRetriever` is based on `user.try(:staff?)`, so anonymous requests can never bypass the 60s Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`. With the loading view reloading every 30s, this can lead to repeated job enqueues while retries are throttled. However, this looks like an intentional policy (only staff bypass throttling) and doesn’t conclusively break correctness from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default of 1 for cook_method backfills all existing posts as raw_html, causing every existing post to render raw markdown uncooked; default must be 0 (regular)

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `Post.cook_methods` as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and the migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`. Nothing in the diff shows that `1` maps to `:raw_html` or that `0` maps to `:regular`; that mapping depends on `Enum` implementation (not shown). The finding asserts a specific numeric mapping/backfill behavior (“all existing posts as raw_html”) that is not verifiable from the diff and is likely a misread given the ordering `:regular, :raw_html`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb uses i.content which is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (they provide description, not content), raising NoMethodError and silently failing the entire feed import since retry is false; needs i.content || i.description fallback

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the job unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil for any feed item, this will raise (nil.scrub / nil passed to unescapeHTML), aborting the job run; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the failed run won’t be retried. The suggested `i.content || i.description` (and/or nil-guard) would prevent this crash for items without `content`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed loading.html.erb reloads forever with no terminal failure state when TopicEmbed remains empty after perform_retrieve (blank embed_by_username, HTTP fetch error, or throttled retrieval), causing infinite reload loop for unretrievable articles

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `embed/loading` (which unconditionally `document.location.reload()` every 30s). There is no terminal state if the embed never gets created. The diff shows multiple paths where `TopicEmbed` can remain empty: `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can be throttled via `retrieved_recently?` (so `perform_retrieve` is skipped), `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early if `embed_by_username` does not map to a user (blank/misconfigured), and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url)` without rescue so HTTP/read errors can prevent creation. In these cases the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely with no failure message/state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key method in poll_feed.rb is dead code - never called, so intended per-feed modification tracking was never wired up and every hourly run re-parses the full feed; should be wired up or deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (lines 18-20 in the new file) but is not referenced anywhere else in the diff (and `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` each run). The "dead code" part is verifiable from this diff; the implied optimization/modification-tracking intent isn’t wired up here, but this is a performance/cleanup concern rather than a clear functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor.rb save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) change affects every revision but has no test coverage in the diff, leaving either normal admin edits or embed imports unverified for validation behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from an unconditional `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which is a nontrivial behavior change affecting all revisions (default path validates; skip_validations bypasses validations). While the new embed import/update flow calls `revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, the added specs (e.g., topic_embed_spec) only assert content changes and do not explicitly cover/verify the new validation-skipping behavior or ensure normal revisions still validate. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js crashes with TypeError when host page omits the 'discourse-comments' div since getElementById returns null and there is no guard before appendChild

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then used immediately: `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no null-check. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb calls post.user.small_avatar_url with no nil guard, causing a 500 in the externally visible iframe if the post author was deleted

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template unconditionally calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username`. If `post.user` were ever `nil` (e.g., if a post can exist without an associated user), this would raise a `NoMethodError` and break the embed iframe rendering. However, the diff does not show whether Discourse guarantees `Post#user` is always present (via DB constraints/validations or user-deletion behavior), so the claimed 500 on deleted authors is plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration adds cook_method with default: 1 (raw_html), so all existing posts default to raw_html and bypass the markdown cooking pipeline, injecting raw markdown and unfiltered inline HTML; default should be 0 (regular)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `cook_method` with `default: 1` and defines `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, but the finding’s core claim—“1 == raw_html so all existing posts bypass cooking/sanitization”—depends on how `Enum.new` maps symbols to integers, which is not shown in this diff. The comment in `Post#cook` (“Default is to cook posts”) suggests the default is intended to be the regular cooking path, not raw HTML, so the asserted mapping/consequence is not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :top_topics gains force: true, which drops and recreates the table on migrate-up, destroying accumulated topic stats — unrelated change bundled with a whitespace edit

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, but the finding’s claim that this will destroy accumulated stats “on migrate-up” for existing installs isn’t supported: Rails migrations are not re-run once applied, so an upgrade won’t drop/recreate an already-migrated `top_topics` table. `force: true` would only drop the table if the migration is executed in an environment where the table already exists (e.g., rerunning the migration), which is not what normal `db:migrate` does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 removes the --category option and category_id plumbing, silently breaking existing thor disqus:import -c users as an unrelated feature deletion

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the `category_id` lookup/plumbing, changing the import path to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` with no category parameter. As a result, `thor disqus:import -c <category>` would no longer accept `-c` (and imported topics can no longer be directed to a category via this command), which is a backwards-incompatible behavioral break introduced by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 changes save to validate: !@opts[:skip_validations], letting any future caller with skip_validations bypass save-time validations — change bundled into this PR without its own requirement

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change PostRevisor behavior: in lib/post_revisor.rb `@post.save` becomes `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning callers can now bypass ActiveRecord validations by passing `skip_validations: true`. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral expansion (and is immediately used by this PR in TopicEmbed.import via `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). Whether this is “wrong” is debatable/intentional for imports, but it’s a legitimate scope/architecture concern rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:22 builds a Redis key "feed-modified:#{sha1}" that is never read or written anywhere — dead code with no implemented etag/modified-since check; delete it

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the new method `feed_key` constructs `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"` but it is not referenced anywhere else in the diff (not used in `execute` or `poll_feed`, and no Redis read/write exists). This is dead/unimplemented scaffolding for caching/etag logic rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returning raw for raw_html posts plus PostCreator accepting arbitrary cook_method means user-visible post content bypasses the cook/sanitize pipeline; TopicEmbed.import uses skip_validations with raw HTML, so unfiltered RSS feed HTML reaches embed/best.html.erb — an unstated expansion of the trust model

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a bypass of the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and `PostCreator` allows setting `post.cook_method` from arbitrary opts (lib/post_creator.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` uses `PostCreator.new(... raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` and appends HTML including a link built from `url` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), while feed content comes from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `i.content`) and is not sanitized. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Together, this means untrusted remote HTML can reach user-visible rendering without the usual cooking/sanitize protections, creating a verifiable XSS/trust-boundary/security defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration default for cook_method is 1 (raw_html) instead of 0 (regular), bypassing the markdown cooking pipeline for all posts

adjudication.rationale: The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1` aligns with Discourse’s existing Enum usage where `Enum.new(:regular, ...)` maps `:regular` to `1` (e.g., `Post.types` uses `:regular` as the first enum value, historically stored as 1). The new `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` therefore makes default `1` correspond to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Raw HTML is only enabled when explicitly set (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb: i.content.scrub crashes the hourly feed poll when a feed item has no content element, skipping remaining items

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` element, `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-iteration and preventing remaining items from being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb: embed_url matched as raw string without canonicalization across three writers, causing duplicate topics for the same article

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed` keys embeds by the raw `embed_url` string: lookup via `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and `topic_id_for_embed` uses exact match, with a unique DB index on `:embed_url`. There is no URL normalization/canonicalization (scheme, trailing slash, tracking params, etc.). Multiple call sites can supply different URL variants (`PollFeed` uses `i.link` or `i.id`; `TopicRetriever` and Disqus import use the URL passed in). This can plausibly create multiple topics for the same underlying article if different URL representations are used, but the diff alone can’t prove it will happen in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb: invalid_host? compares raw site setting to URI#host, so entering a scheme in embeddable_host disables embedding entirely

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, invalid_host? does a strict string compare: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. `URI(...).host` returns only the hostname (e.g., `eviltrout.com`), so if an admin configures `embeddable_host` with a scheme (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com`), the comparison will always fail and `retrieve` will never call `perform_retrieve`, effectively disabling embedding for that configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed loading page reloads every 30s with no terminal failure state, creating an unbounded reload/enqueue loop

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no embed exists (`topic_id` is nil), it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `embed/loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(document.location.reload(), 30000)` in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails or `TopicEmbed.import_remote` can't create the post), the page will keep reloading indefinitely and keep enqueueing `retrieve_topic` on every reload, creating an unbounded reload/enqueue loop with no terminal failure state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb: check-then-insert on embed_url without rescue on unique index causes RecordNotUnique crash under concurrent imports

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(... embed_url: url ...)` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Under concurrent imports of the same URL, two workers can both observe no row and then race to `create!`, causing the loser to raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique (no rescue/retry shown in the diff), which can crash the job/request path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb: feed_key is a phantom method—computed but never read, describing cache invalidation that never happens

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (memoizing a Redis/cache key based on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced anywhere in the diff. There is no logic that reads/writes this key to track last-modified/ETag or otherwise prevent unnecessary polling, so the method is effectively dead code and suggests an incomplete caching/invalidation implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) with no timeout, size limit, or content-type check on a path reachable from unauthenticated traffic

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches via `open-uri` without any timeout, size limit, or content-type validation. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, it does `open(url).read` (lib used by `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`), and `EmbedController#best` can enqueue retrieval based on `params[:embed_url]` for non-authenticated requests (no auth filter shown). Even though `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` restricts the host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the request is still attacker-triggerable (via the public embed endpoint) and can hang or download unbounded content, leading to DoS/resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb: content_sha1 is updated even when revise! is a no-op, desynchronizing the change-detection key

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` but ignores its return value and unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it early-returns when `should_revise?` is false), so the embed’s change-detection key can be advanced even if the post wasn’t actually updated, preventing future updates from being detected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb sets default: 1 for cook_method, which maps to :raw_html in the Enum, so all posts default to raw_html and skip the cooking/rendering pipeline; default should be 0

adjudication.rationale: In `Post.cook_methods`, the enum is declared as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, so the first value (`:regular`) maps to the default, not `:raw_html`. The migration sets `cook_method` default to `1`, and elsewhere in this codebase enums like `Post.types` are also defined with `Enum.new(:regular, ...)`, strongly implying `1` corresponds to `:regular` (the normal path) rather than `:raw_html`. Nothing in the diff shows that `1` maps to `:raw_html` or that “all posts default to raw_html and skip cooking”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114-117 silently removes the --category option and category_id wiring from the Disqus import task, breaking existing scripts using -c and dropping category-scoped imports without migration path

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the `category_id` lookup and wiring into `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)`. The import path is changed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass any category. This will break existing scripts that use `-c/--category` (Thor will reject the option) and removes previously supported category-scoped imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 edits an already-shipped migration to add force: true, which would drop and recreate top_topics on environments re-running it, destroying computed stats data; plus unrelated whitespace-only edits to migrate_word_counts.rb

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can destroy any previously computed `top_topics` data in scenarios where the migration is re-run (e.g., rollback/re-migrate, or migrating against a DB that already has the table). The whitespace-only change in `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` is present but is just formatting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:11-15 introduces a skip_validations option in the shared post revision path as an unflagged drive-by change, creating risk that future callers bypass validations on unrelated edits

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, introducing a new `skip_validations` escape hatch on the shared post revision path. This is a broad behavioral change (callers of `revise!` can now bypass validations) and, while used intentionally here by `TopicEmbed.import` (`revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`), it does create a maintainability/safety risk for future or unrelated callers. It’s a real, diff-grounded review concern but not a directly verifiable defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: RSS/imported content is stored with cook_method :raw_html, skips the sanitization pipeline, and is rendered with raw in best.html.erb, allowing script execution from attacker-controlled feed/article HTML

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a :raw_html cook method that bypasses the rendering/sanitization pipeline (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Imported feed/article content is stored using this mode (`TopicEmbed.import` passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)`), and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). For raw_html posts, `post.cooked` will be the unsanitized attacker-controlled HTML, enabling stored XSS via RSS/remote imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed passes i.content.scrub (UTF-8 fix only) into import with no tag filtering; Readability allowlist only applies in import_remote

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, feed item HTML is taken from `i.content.scrub` (then `CGI.unescapeHTML`) and passed directly to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization/allowlist. `TopicEmbed.import` stores it via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The Readability allowlist (`tags`, `attributes`) is only applied in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, not in PollFeed. This is a verifiable XSS/vector defect when importing untrusted feed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML/attribute injection: unescaped attacker-supplied URL interpolated into single-quoted href in imported_from footer, allowing stored XSS via crafted URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet containing `#{url}` directly into `contents` (no escaping), with only a weak validation `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. A crafted URL containing a single quote and additional attributes (e.g., `http://x.com' onmouseover='...`) would break out of the single-quoted `href` and inject attacker-controlled attributes/HTML. This is then stored and rendered as raw HTML (`cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw`), making it a stored XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: JS injection: user-controlled request.referer interpolated unescaped into a JavaScript string literal in embed.html.erb; should use j()/JSON encoding of a validated value
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: the unescaped request.referer header is inserted into JavaScript in a template (embed.html.erb), enabling XSS/JS injection. Candidate also suggests proper escaping/encoding (j()/JSON) consistent with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization bypass: embed_controller relies solely on client-controlled Referer header to gate access to embed topics, trivially spoofable, allowing cross-origin reads

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes access solely by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then sets `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`. Because `Referer` is a client-controlled header, a caller can spoof it to pass the check and fetch the embedded topic HTML (`/embed/best?embed_url=...`) even when not actually coming from the allowed embedding site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open-uri SSRF pattern: poll_feed and TopicRetriever open URLs with no scheme/protocol validation at fetch site; open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, and future callers of import_remote inherit an unrestricted fetch primitive
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe an SSRF risk from using open/open-uri to fetch a URL without validating/whitelisting it. The candidate explicitly mentions poll_feed opening URLs with no scheme/protocol validation and unrestricted redirects, which matches the golden issue of PollFeed calling open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and allowing arbitrary internal/external fetches if the setting is attacker-controlled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: advisory: embed.js origin check uses indexOf substring match instead of exact equality, allowing related-but-untrusted origins to pass and forge postMessage (e.g., resize frame)
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security issue: origin validation relies on indexOf/substring matching rather than strict origin equality, which can be bypassed by a malicious domain that contains the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com), allowing untrusted postMessage origins to pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb: only test of PollFeed#poll_feed stubs poll_feed itself, so SimpleRSS parsing, URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import are never exercised; nil content in Atom items raises NoMethodError and with retry: false kills the whole run untested

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, it unconditionally calls `i.content.scrub` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). If an RSS/Atom item lacks `content` (i.e., `i.content` is nil), this will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the polling run, preventing subsequent items from being imported. This behavior is directly implied by the code. The spec file only tests `execute` and never exercises `poll_feed`, so this failure mode would not be caught by the added tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb: tests stub retrieved_recently? so the actual redis setnx/expire throttle and no_throttle staff bypass are never executed; throttle regressions pass all tests

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the two “with a valid host” examples explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false, and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. That means the real throttle implementation in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (the `$redis.setnx`/`expire` logic) and the `@opts[:no_throttle]` bypass path are never exercised by these tests. This is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a runtime defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb: 'Supports updating the post' never verifies embed.content_sha1 is updated; a regression to a no-op would cause re-revision on every poll while the test still passes

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, updates are gated by comparing the new `content_sha1` to `embed.content_sha1`, and on change it calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after revising the post. The spec `it "Supports updating the post"` (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) only asserts that `post.cooked` contains the new contents, and never asserts that the persisted TopicEmbed row’s `content_sha1` was updated. A regression that removed/failed the `update_column` would not be caught and could cause repeated revisions on subsequent polls even though this test still passes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb: no test for the no-change branch (content_sha1 equality → skip revision) that protects against duplicate revisions on every PollFeed run

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a no-change guard in `TopicEmbed.import` (only revises when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, otherwise it skips `PostRevisor`), which is important to prevent repeated revisions on repeated imports (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` calling `TopicEmbed.import` every run). The new spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` covers creation and the change/update path, but it does not cover the equality/no-change branch to assert that `PostRevisor#revise!` is not called and `content_sha1` is not updated when contents are identical. This is a specific missing-test issue tied to newly added logic, not a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:46-51: 'creates a topic view' only asserts mock TopicView.new call args; rendered embed content (post.cooked, small_avatar_url via best.html.erb) is never verified with real data

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the "creates a topic view" example only sets an expectation on `TopicView.new(123, nil, {best: 5})` and then calls `get :best`; it does not exercise the `embed/best.html.erb` rendering path with real `@topic_view.posts`/`post.user.small_avatar_url`/`raw post.cooked`. This is a concrete gap in coverage for the newly added embed view behavior, but not a verifiable functional defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:7-9: test named 'is 404 without an embed_url' only asserts response.should_not be_success; any 400/5xx satisfies it, so the test name misrepresents what is checked

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the example is named "is 404 without an embed_url" but the assertion is only `response.should_not be_success` after `get :best` (no explicit status check). That means any non-2xx (e.g., 400/422/500) would satisfy the test, so the name overstates what is verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb: no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) branch and args[:user_id] lookup have no test coverage; non-staff throttling regression would be invisible to CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` with new branching logic: it conditionally looks up `User.where(id: args[:user_id]).first` and passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. There are new specs for `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, `PollFeed`, and `TopicEmbed`, but none for `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, and the `TopicRetriever` spec stubs `retrieved_recently?` rather than exercising throttle behavior or the `no_throttle` option. So the staff/non-staff throttle pathway and user_id lookup introduced here are not covered by CI tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131219203905 adds cook_method with default 1 (:raw_html), silently reclassifying every existing post as raw_html so cooked output returns raw markdown; default should be 0 (:regular) with importer passing raw_html explicitly

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and a migration setting `cook_method` default to `1`. But the finding assumes `1` maps to `:raw_html`; that mapping is not shown in the diff, and existing code (`Post.types ||= Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`) strongly suggests `Enum.new` likely assigns `:regular` to `1` (as commonly done in this codebase), meaning default `1` would be `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. Additionally, the importer explicitly passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`, so raw_html is opt-in for imported posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131223171005 edits an already-shipped migration to add force: true to create_table :top_topics, making re-runs destructive and causing schema drift between fresh and upgraded installs

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration file (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which would drop/recreate the table if the migration were ever re-run (e.g., reset/rollback + re-migrate), making it potentially destructive. However, from the diff alone it's not verifiable that this causes “schema drift between fresh and upgraded installs,” since on a normal fresh migrate the table wouldn’t exist and `force: true` yields the same schema as without it; the primary issue is the risky change to an already-existing migration and destructive behavior on re-runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20131217174004 uses force: true on new table topic_embeds, turning accidental re-execution into a silent DROP of all embed mappings; force: true should be omitted

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`. `force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, which can lead to data loss if the migration is re-run or applied in an environment where the table exists. This is a valid migration-safety concern, though not a guaranteed runtime defect in normal one-time migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds has no FK on topic_id/post_id and update path runs update_column outside transaction, allowing orphaned rows that permanently block re-import and break TopicView for that embed URL

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_id` and `post_id` as plain integers with only a unique index on `embed_url` (no foreign keys), and the model associations (`belongs_to :topic`, `belongs_to :post`) do not specify any dependent cleanup. That means deleting a Topic/Post can leave orphaned `topic_embeds` rows. The code then trusts those rows: `topic_id_for_embed` blindly returns `topic_id` (could break `EmbedController#best` when building `TopicView`), and the update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` which will blow up if `post` is nil, effectively preventing re-import because the orphan row with unique `embed_url` remains. The finding’s specific linkage to `update_column` being outside a transaction is less direct, but the core orphan/blocking behavior is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:33 - i.content raises NoMethodError on RSS feeds lacking a content element (only description), killing the poll run; with retry: false and no rescue/logging the failure is invisible and causes silent partial imports

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the import loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common for RSS feeds that only provide `description`), `i.content` will be `nil`, and calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-run. The file sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and has no rescue around the loop, so this exception will stop polling/importing for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:30-38 - redis throttle key is set via setnx before retrieval succeeds, so a failed fetch leaves subsequent retry jobs no-op 'successfully' for 60 seconds

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? sets the Redis key via $redis.setnx and $redis.expire before perform_retrieve runs (retrieve calls perform_retrieve unless ... retrieved_recently?). If perform_retrieve (or downstream fetch_http/import_remote) fails or returns early, the throttle key still blocks further retrieval attempts for 60 seconds. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/behavior concern, but it may be intentional throttling rather than a strict correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:58 and poll_feed.rb:27 - open(url) used without timeout or read size caps, so slow/large remote hosts hang Sidekiq workers indefinitely; feed poller also downloads unbounded documents with no memory guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded remote fetches using Ruby's open-uri without any explicit timeouts or size limits: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`. As written, a slow or very large response can block a Sidekiq worker and/or consume excessive memory, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb:6-10 - embed iframe unconditionally reloads every 30s forever with no attempt counter, terminal state, or error signal, so permanent retrieval failures leave 'Loading Discussion...' endlessly

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the inline script calls document.location.reload() inside setTimeout every 30000ms with no stop condition, attempt counter, or success/failure check. Since this template is rendered when no topic_id is found (EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic then renders 'loading'), any permanent retrieval failure will keep the client reloading indefinitely and repeatedly hitting the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32-34 - non-HTTP feed item links are silently substituted with i.id and then dropped with no log, error, or counter, making polling a silent no-op for feeds using non-URL ids

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, the item URL is set to `i.link` and then replaced with `i.id` when blank or non-http(s) (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). However, TopicEmbed.import immediately returns unless the URL matches `^https?\:\/\/` (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). So for feeds where `link` is missing/non-http and `id` is a non-URL identifier (common for Atom GUIDs), the item will be silently skipped with no logging or counters, making polling effectively do nothing for those entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:22-24, 41-44 - update_column(:content_sha1) runs unconditionally even when revise! returns false, advancing the hash cursor past actual stored content so genuine later upstream edits are treated as already applied and never imported

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed is updated (content_sha1 differs), it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking whether `revise!` actually performed an update or returned false (e.g., `should_revise?` short-circuits). This can desynchronize `topic_embeds.content_sha1` from the actual post content, causing later real changes to be skipped because the cursor hash was advanced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:23-27 - feed_key ('feed-modified:...') is defined but never used anywhere in the diff, dead code implying unimplemented ETag/Last-Modified conditional fetching

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method is introduced (computing `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) but there is no usage of `feed_key` anywhere else in the provided diff. The job’s `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without any conditional GET/Last-Modified/ETag logic or Redis lookup, so `feed_key` is currently dead code and suggests an incomplete implementation.
